[266] Drag and Drop Shifts on the Grid
epics.description: Use drag and drop actions on the grid to move shifts PRD - https://docs.google.com/document/d/1nLbkSOuf8Cx6Jk9zR3cD8iBkFv_zQLexGNqVCiB67YI/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.wiklgl6fia8k UX Link - https://shiftmanager-262-scope-ca916c26db1e.herokuapp.com/ Drag and Drop Shift Templates Capability The Problem: Managers and shift planners often spend hours manually typing out shift details—such as start times, end times, roles, and break durations—for every single employee on a weekly or monthly schedule. This repetitive, manual data entry is incredibly tedious and highly prone to human error. A simple typo can result in understaffing, overlapping shifts, or an employee showing up at the wrong time, which ultimately impacts business operations and employee satisfaction. The Solution: Introduce a sidebar or menu of pre-configured shift templates (e.g., "Morning Cashier: 8 AM - 4 PM" or "Night Shift: 10 PM - 6 AM") alongside the main calendar grid. Users can simply click on a specific template, drag it across the screen, and drop it directly into the desired cell (representing an employee and a specific date) on the scheduling grid to instantly assign that exact shift. User Story - As a schedule manager, I want to drag and drop pre-configured shift templates directly onto specific employee rows and date columns within the scheduling grid, So that I can build accurate schedules faster, eliminate manual typing errors, and visually confirm coverage in real-time. Acceptance Criteria: Template Availability & Drag Initiation Given the user is viewing the scheduling grid When they look at the template sidebar/menu Then they should see a list of pre-configured shift templates And clicking and holding a template should immediately pick it up and attach a visual representation of the shift to the cursor. 2. Visual Feedback During Drag (Hover State) Given the user is dragging a shift template across the screen When the cursor hovers over a valid cell (intersecting an employee row and a date column) on the scheduling grid Then the targeted cell should highlight or visually indicate that it is ready to receive the drop. 3. Successful Drop & Assignment Given the user is hovering a dragged template over a valid grid cell When the user releases the mouse button (drops the template) Then a new shift block matching the template's details (start time, end time, role) should instantly appear in that cell And the shift should be automatically assigned to the corresponding employee on that specific date And the schedule data should save automatically. 4. Invalid Drop Location Given the user is dragging a shift template When the user releases the mouse button outside of a valid scheduling grid cell (e.g., on the navigation bar or empty space) Then the template should visually snap back to its origin in the sidebar And no new shift should be created on the schedule. 5. Handling Pre-existing Shifts (Conflict) Given a user drags a template over a cell that already contains a scheduled shift When the user drops the template Then the system should either add the new shift alongside the existing one (if multiple shifts per day are allowed) or display a prompt warning the user of a shift conflict.

epics.description: The EPIC focuses on adding search and filter capabilities on the coverage grid. PRD - https://docs.google.com/document/d/1TM5AZoHXifT2ioIeAOaeS17ufcnpDE-ZhGURoYWYfqc/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.wiklgl6fia8k UX Link - https://shiftmanager-262-scope-ca916c26db1e.herokuapp.com/ Advanced Filters and Search Capability The Problem: Schedulers often struggle to isolate relevant data amidst thousands of shift records. Finding specific skills, rule violations, or coverage gaps requires navigating multiple screens or scrolling endlessly. The Solution: A granular filtering allowing multi-select criteria such as Service Territory, Job Profile, Skills, Custom Objects, Request Types, Violations, Status, Shift Template combined with a "Smart Object Search" helps narrow down the results for effective review and updates. User Story: As a Planner When I am viewing a schedule board populated with hundreds of shifts and resources. I want to instantly isolate specific subsets of data (e.g., finding all Electricians in NY or finding a specific employee by name). So that I can focus on relevant information and make targeted updates without scrolling through irrelevant data. Acceptance Criteria - P0. Ability to save and retrieve filters: Users should be able to save the filters they create and easily retrieve them. they should also be able to persist their filter as default filter everytime they load the shift ui. They should also be able to provide a name to their filters eg. team 1 etc. 1. UI & Filter Accessibility Scenario: Accessing the filtering interface Given the user is viewing the schedule or shift list, When they click the "Filter" icon or expand the filter panel, Then they are presented with a "Smart Object Search" bar at the top. And they see collapsible/expandable sections for granular multi-select filters: Service Territory, Service Resource, Job Profile, Skills, Custom Objects, Request Types, and Violations. 2. Multi-Select Filtering Logic Scenario: Selecting criteria within the same category (OR logic) Given the user is using the granular filters, When they select multiple options within the same category (e.g., selecting both "Dispatcher" and "Technician" under Job Profile), Then the results update to show shifts/resources matching any of the selected options (Job Profile = Dispatcher OR Technician). Scenario: Selecting criteria across different categories (AND logic) Given the user is using the granular filters, When they select options across different categories (e.g., Service Territory = "North Region" AND Skills = "Electrical"), Then the results update to show only shifts/resources that match all the selected cross-category criteria. Scenario: Filtering by Request Types and Violations Given the user is managing exceptions on the schedule, When they filter by "Request Types" (e.g., PTO, Shift Swap), Then the view filters to display only resources or shifts that have pending or approved requests of those types. When they filter by "Violations" (e.g., Overtime, Rest Period Violation), Then the view highlights and isolates shifts or schedules currently triggering those specific rule violations. 3. Smart Object Search Logic Scenario: Using the Smart Object Search Given the user is looking for a specific record or keyword, When they type text into the "Smart Object Search" bar (e.g., a resource's name, a specific shift ID, or a custom object reference), Then the system dynamically searches across all indexed fields and related objects on the schedule. And the results instantly narrow down to display only the schedules, resources, or shifts containing that text string. Scenario: Combining Smart Search with Granular Filters Given the user has applied multi-select filters (e.g., Territory = "East"), When they type a keyword into the "Smart Object Search", Then the search string is applied only to the currently filtered dataset, further narrowing down the results. 4. Custom Objects Support Scenario: Filtering by Custom Objects Given the user's organizational setup includes custom objects tied to shifts or resources (e.g., "Vehicle Type" or "Project Code"), When they open the filter panel, Then these custom objects appear as selectable filter categories dynamically based on the system configuration. 5. Managing Filters Scenario: Clearing filters and search Given the user has applied multiple filters and a Smart Object Search string, When they click the "Clear All" or "Reset" button, Then all checkboxes are cleared, the search bar is emptied, and the schedule view returns to its default, unfiltered state. And the user can remove individual filter tags by clicking an 'x' next to the applied filter pill without clearing the entire board.

epics.name: Auto Refresh of Gantt
epics.description: To ensure that planners and schedule managers viewing the Gantt chart always see the most up-to-date schedule. The Gantt UI must automatically refresh without manual user intervention when relevant scheduling records are created, updated, or deleted in the background. The Gantt chart must listen for and react to background database changes (Create, Update, Delete) on the following objects: Service Appointment, Service Resource, Shift, Resource Absence, Service Territory Member, Job Profile. The UI should only refresh or re-render records if the background change belongs to the current filtering criteria. (date/time, field filters) Changes outside the user's current view should be ignored to save processing power and bandwidth. The refresh must not interrupt a planner who is actively dragging/dropping/updating a record or editing a modal. If a background update modifies a record currently visible on the screen, a brief visual indicator (e.g., a subtle highlight or flash) should denote that the record has been updated. NFR: The auto-refresh listener must not degrade the initial load time of the Gantt chart.

epics.name: [266] Shift Rotation
epics.description: Contact center schedulers need a way to define a repeating shift rotation pattern (e.g., Morning → Afternoon → Night) and assign agents to it, so that when a roster is generated for any date range, each agent is automatically placed on the correct shift based on where they are in the rotation cycle, without the scheduler having to manually track or calculate individual agent positions. HLD - https://docs.google.com/document/d/14w6oSdvGcogCaTd5UFyg6bqKiD5aWrWjIjvbkytjPNg/edit?tab=t.0 Product Vision A scheduler generates shifts from a repeating pattern and gets them filled, on demand, for any date range, without hand-building each schedule or babysitting a background job. Problem Today there is no clean way to (1) fill pattern-generated shifts automatically under a chosen policy (2) rotate resources through shift classes over time so no one is stuck on let’s say nights, or (3) reuse a hand-built roster across date ranges. Solution Manual and Automatic resource-selection modes from a single Rotation Builder.

epics.name: 264 SFS [Trust] Feature Toggle Cleanup
epics.description: 264 SFS [Trust] Feature Toggle Cleanup Dedicated epic for the 264-cycle feature toggle cleanup effort — carry-over from W-21962794 ( * [262][Trust][Scheduling Intelligence] , Closed). Spawned from the FT plan documented in docs/LLM/o2-workspace/docs/LLM/264/ft/README.md . Author: Guy Eden · Owner: Yonatan Bar-Yehuda · Quality: Irad Ben Dosa One-sentence summary We are simplifying version-gated feature toggles in the O2 stack by agreeing on MpVersion 258.0.0 as the floor for production traffic, which lets us delete roughly two-thirds of the toggle predicates and remove the matching if (FT.isEnabled()) branches from 5 Java repos. Why it matters Reduced complexity. Every FT predicate is a live branch in production. 25 of them have been effectively always-on for ~6 months and are now dead weight. Deleting them cuts regression-surface area in the request and response translators. Clearer version contract. MpVersion and CoreApiVersion flow from the caller as HTTP headers → RequestContextDTO (app-infra) → MDC → FeatureToggle.isFeatureEnabled(...) . Each service parses them independently; the MpVersion ↔ CoreApiVersion mapping lives in the external FT service, not in O2 source. Fewer predicates means fewer places where a mismatch can produce a silent misfire. Unblocks v262+ work. Features gated FROM 262.0.0 ( ExcludeArrivalWindowRulesForReshuffle , ScheduleOperationRemoveTasksFromGanttBug ) need a matching CoreApiVersion(67) predicate added. Doing that while the table is still cluttered with stale 238.3 / 240.x / 244 gates was not defensible. Phases — what's done, what's in flight, what's planned Done in 262 ( W-21962794 , Closed) Existing-status enumeration: 39 features × 4 prod regions, predicates documented per region. Splunk validation that production traffic is at MpVersion ≥ 258.0.0 across all 4 regions. Automation scripts: utils/promote_to_enable.py (Playwright-driven 25-feature × 4-region console flip with backup JSON) and utils/backout_to_custom.py (revert tool with dry-run-by-default). Pre-flip JSON dumps of all 4 prod regions ( jsons/ft_prod{1,3,4,8}_*.json ). FeatureToggleConfig.json 258-floor sweep — landed in common #3132 . In flight (4 PRs, console-flip side) | Repo | PR | Scope | |---|---|---| | o2service-common | #3132 | ABRequiredTimeZoneParam, TerritoryOptimizationRequestNewFields, ReadonlyFSLEndpoint, ComplexWorkAdvanced header, FeatureToggleConfig.json 258-floor | | o2-data-translator-service | #969 | 10 Easy features: ScheduleMode, ComplexWorkSlidingOverLunchBreak, CustomerLabelsParametersEnhancement, KeepScheduledServices, OffsetInSeconds, EnableReshuffleOnScheduleAndAB, ABRequiredTimeZoneParam, AllowOvertimeImprovements, AllowOvertimeInMiddleOfShift, PreferGPUEngine | | o2-fetch-data-service | #421 | ComplexWorkAdvanced, ParallelMSW | | o2service | #3126 | FillResourceGapsRequest, KeepScheduledServices (svc side) | To-do — 10 carry-over child stories under THIS epic Total story points: 23 (≈ XL T-shirt for the FT cleanup portion). Sequencing rules Console flips before code cleanup. Removing a source-side branch first would force the enabled path for any sub-258 client. 5-day observation window between flipping the console in all 4 regions and merging the per-feature code-cleanup PRs. Hard features ( ResourceContinuousAvailability , SALifeCycle ) get dedicated PRs with human integration testing. Yaml model regen runs only after the matching if (FT.isEnabled()) branches are gone. Operational artifacts Forward script: python docs/LLM/264/ft/utils/promote_to_enable.py --env prod{1,3,4,8} — 25-feature × 1-region console flip per run. Back-out script (immediate): python docs/LLM/264/ft/utils/backout_to_custom.py --env prod1 --apply . Recommended sequencing: dev4 → perf1 → test1 → (observe) → prod1 → prod3 → prod4 → prod8 . Stakeholders Implementor: Guy Eden Validator: Yonatan Bar-Yehuda QA Engineer: Irad Ben Dosa Approver / Code review: Orelie Fridler + team

266 SFS Frontline AI - NGA agent_router Routing Reliability
epics.description: Description — Target Customer and Benefit / Goal The Field Mobile Worker agent on NGA (New Agentforce Builder) ships three team-owned subagents wired to a single agent_router : TroubleshootingForMobileWorker , PostWorkSummary , and InteractivePreWorkBriefForFieldService . In production we observe intermittent misrouting — the router transitions to the wrong subagent, particularly when subagent instructions/descriptions overlap. Source-level review of chatbots/module-graph-runtime ( RouterNode / FlashClassifier ) confirmed the headline finding : the router's reasoning.instructions block does not enter the classifier call. Routing is a tool-call where the LLM sees exactly one string per subagent — NodeReference.description . Overlap in those descriptions is the direct cause of misroutes; no prose added to router-level reasoning.instructions can fix it. This epic delivers the concrete authoring + platform changes that actually move the needle: (1) rewrite the three team-owned subagent descriptions using the PostWorkSummary structure as a template, (2) add available when guards to go_to_* transitions using existing page-context and a new WorkOrderStatus variable, (3) pin the router to sfdc_ai__DefaultEinsteinHyperClassifier , and (4) run an eight-utterance evaluation suite covering the ambiguity zones. Source document: W-22860883 — NGA agent_router Routing Reliability Exploration (local copy: ~/Documents/claude/W-22860883-router-exploration.md ). Parent work item: W-22860883 . Acceptance Criteria Three team-owned subagent descriptions rewritten to follow PostWorkSummary structure: name the audience (field worker), the entity (work order / product / asset), the lifecycle stage (pre-arrival / in-progress / completed), 3+ positive utterance examples, explicit "Do NOT use" section referencing sibling subagents. available when guards added to go_to_InteractivePreWorkBriefForFieldService , go_to_TroubleshootingForMobileWorker , and go_to_PostWorkSummary transitions on the router. Router model_config.model pinned to sfdc_ai__DefaultEinsteinHyperClassifier (currently unset — falls back to org-default reasoner). Eight-utterance evaluation suite (§7 of the source doc) passes on the updated agent, measured either via sfdc.co/agentscript-dev live editor or a scratch-org deploy. ROUTER_CLASSIFIER_CHOICES span attribute is observable in Splunk/Argus for post-deploy verification in prod. Legacy Agent Builder Classic path continues to work (regression parity) — verified via W-22933766 Suite 2. Known Dependencies / Risks Dependency — sfdc_fieldservice__FieldServiceMobileWork template ownership. The description rewrites modify the template itself. Confirm sole SFS Frontline AI ownership vs. shared with other cloud teams (Niv Garber / #nga-template-migration ). Dependency — WorkOrderStatus variable population. Path 2 available when guards require a new agent variable populated via before_reasoning_iteration reading WorkOrder.Status off currentRecordId . Product-level decision required. Dependency — observability access. ROUTER_CLASSIFIER_CHOICES span attribute visibility in prod Splunk/Argus (Olivier Martin / Nico Pappagianis). Risk — customer-authored neighboring subagents. Org-specific subagents next to ours cannot be enumerated in advance. Description rewrites defend by naming entity + lifecycle stage explicitly (§4.2 of source doc). Risk — currentObjectApiName may be blank in messaging-only sessions. Path 1 weak guards silently disappear subagents if the variable is unset. Verify populate-timing before adopting. Out of Scope Legacy Topic Selector / SOMA path — not in scope; the router covered here is NGA RouterNode only. additional_parameter__enable_serial_tool_state_chaining (Lever H) — not source-confirmed; deferred pending Stefan Krawczyk clarification. Router-level reasoning.instructions rewrite (Lever F) — confirmed no-op per §3.3 of source doc. Customer-authored subagent audits — customer orgs own their own subagents. Definition of Done PO has accepted the epic All child WIs closed and their ACs met Description rewrites reviewed with template co-owners Eight-utterance eval suite green on the updated agent ROUTER_CLASSIFIER_CHOICES span visible in prod for post-deploy monitoring Regression: Classic path preview (W-22933766 Suite 2) still passes Resources Source exploration doc: W-22860883 router exploration Parent WI: W-22860883 Runtime engine: chatbots/module-graph-runtime ( RouterNode , FlashClassifier ) Compiler: chatbots/agent-dsl Sibling implementation reference: FieldService Scheduling Agent on NGA (Niv Garber, June 2026) Support channels: #agentscript-dev , #technical-support-new-agent-builder-and-script

epics.name: 266 SFS Frontline AI - [Android] Merge Offline Voice to Form into main branch
epics.description: Voice to Form (V2F) offline is built as a pilot in a separate feature branch. As on-device models improve, mid- and high-tier device penetration grows in the FSL install base, and pilot usage signals demand, we see a path to GA'ing offline V2F. To de-risk that path and unblock parallel work on master, we will merge the offline V2F feature branch back into master and keep the functionality behind a feature flag (off by default). This protects existing V2F online behavior for all customers while allowing the pilot cohort — and future GA rollout — to be controlled via flag/entitlement without maintaining a long-lived divergent branch. In scope: - Rebase and merge the offline V2F feature branch into master; resolve conflicts. - Wrap all offline V2F entry points, model loading, and offline sync paths behind a feature flag (default OFF for all orgs). - Ensure zero behavior change for online V2F when the flag is OFF. - Update CI so offline V2F unit + integration tests run on master. - Migrate any pilot-specific config/telemetry to flag-gated code paths. - Documentation: internal enablement notes for the flag and how to toggle for pilots. Out of scope: - Enabling the flag for any production org (handled via separate LAP/enablement work). - Model updates, UX enhancements, or new-language support (tracked under separate epics). - Public documentation / release notes (deferred until GA epic). Success criteria: - Feature branch fully merged into master with zero unresolved conflicts. - CI green on master post-merge across unit, integration, and offline sync test suites. - Flag OFF: online V2F behavior byte-for-byte identical to pre-merge master (verified by regression pass). - Flag ON in a pilot org: offline V2F end-to-end scenario passes (record → offline → sync). - No open P0/P1 regressions attributable to the merge two weeks post-merge. - Feature branch retired; all downstream offline V2F stories rebase on master.

epics.name: 264 [AGX] New Cards & Enhancements
epics.description: This epic covers the new AGX cards and enhancements delivered for the 264 release across both mobile platforms — iOS and Android . Both platforms implement the same set of guided-experience cards to parity, so a single job flow renders consistently regardless of device. New Cards Location — View a single location (address, latitude/longitude, etc.) and get directions to it. [Code exists from a previous team; refactored to match the AGX card pattern.] Contact — View a single contact record and reach the individual directly via phone, text, or email. [New card] Confirm Record Details — View and confirm the fields of a single record, used as a gating mechanism to track progress through the guided experience. [Shares code with the Record Detail card; wired to the card status update when the user taps Confirm.] Data Capture Form List — Complete a collection of Data Capture forms, assigned to a record by non-admin users. [New card] Work Plan — Embed a Work Plan within the job flow, allowing non-admin users to add or remove actions via the Work Plan. [Code exists from a previous team; refactored to match the AGX card pattern.] Related List of Attachments — View a list of file attachments associated with a given record. [New card] Enhancements Data Capture Form — Enhance the existing card to accept the Visit object as input, enabling forms parented by Visit. Additionally, support generating PDF reports after a form is completed (consistent with the Form tab). Service Document — Add SR 2.0 support on Visits. Enhance the existing card to launch Service Reports 1.0, and expand the document-template selector to allow choosing Service Reports 1.0. References Figma: AGX Mobile Specs Canvas: Slack Canvas

epics.name: 264 [Workforce Scheduling GA] Additional Cards
epics.description: Synopsis: This epic expands the AGX interface to support a wider range of field service features by adding 11 new cards (such as Location, Contact, Confirm Record Details, Work Plan, and ESRI maps) and enhancing 2 existing ones (Data Capture Form and Service Document). Acceptance Criteria: Admins must be able to configure these new and updated components within AGX flows. The cards must perform their respective functions, such as launching mapping applications, initiating calls or texts, and generating PDF reports from Data Capture Forms or Service Documents. Basic Testing Criteria: Verify that each card displays properly in the mobile interface. Test interactive properties (e.g., tapping the "Call" button on the Contact card, "Get Directions" on the Location card) and ensure the enhanced cards successfully generate PDFs.

epics.name: [AGX GA] Screen Debugging
epics.description: Synopsis: A feature providing admins with a quick and easy way to simulate and debug their AGX screen configurations in high fidelity via the mobile app, without needing an actual root record or production context. Acceptance Criteria: Admins can launch the preview via a QR code scanned on their mobile device. The tool must allow admins to manually set input variables to simulate conditions, view a feed containing the resolved values (such as data flow outputs, properties, and errors), and clearly show when a screen evaluates as "completed". Basic Testing Criteria: Scan the QR code to launch the debug session, input manual variables, and verify that the screen behaves accordingly. Check that the history feed accurately updates with resolved values and captures any generated errors.

epics.name: [AGX GA] Conditional Visibility
epics.description: Synopsis: Enables admins to define business rules that dynamically hide or display specific cards within an AGX screen as the user inputs data or progresses through their work. Acceptance Criteria: Admins can use connected AGX Screen Data Flows to dictate card visibility. Hidden cards must not prevent the user from completing the screen, and previously completed cards must not be hidden. Basic Testing Criteria: Configure an AGX screen where a secondary card only appears if a specific input is provided in the first card. Test that the screen can still be completed if the condition is not met (and the card remains hidden), and verify completed cards stay visible.

epics.name: [AGX GA] Instrumentation
epics.description: Synopsis: The creation of an internal dashboard designed to gather and display usage data on how customers interact with the AGX interface. Acceptance Criteria: The dashboard must visually communicate metrics including how users complete the experience, when and which steps are completed, the duration of each step, the frequency of "escape hatch" usage, and overall user sentiment. Basic Testing Criteria: Simulate various user behaviors on the mobile app, including normal step completion, long durations on a single step, and utilizing the escape hatch. Check the dashboard to verify that this data is accurately captured and reported.

epics.name: [AGX GA] Iteration of Steps
epics.description: Synopsis: Allows an AGX flow to dynamically loop through a series of steps based on a collection of Salesforce records (such as multiple Work Order Line Items), enabling the completion of multiple goals within a single appointment. Acceptance Criteria: Admins must be able to define an iterator within their AGX configuration that establishes which steps and decisions repeat for each item in the data collection. Mobile users must see a dynamic number of screens reflecting the goals present for that specific job. Basic Testing Criteria: Assign a job that has multiple child records associated with it. Ensure the guided flow correctly repeats the assigned iteration loop for every individual child record before permitting the user to proceed to the next stage.

epics.name: [AGX GA] Optional Actions
epics.description: Synopsis: Provides mobile workers with a curated list of optional actions (like launching Data Capture Forms, Quick Actions, or Screen Flows) available throughout the job to handle unplanned deviations without leaving the guided experience. Acceptance Criteria: Admins can configure the order, naming, and availability of both global and record-based actions in this list, incorporating custom business logic to define which records launch the actions. Mobile users can access these actions without needing to use the "escape hatch" to navigate the standard data model. Basic Testing Criteria: Configure an optional action list with a Quick Action and a Data Capture form. Initiate a job on mobile, open the optional actions menu mid-flow, execute an action, and verify the user seamlessly returns to their main job flow upon completion.

epics.name: [AGX GA] Parallel Steps
epics.description: Synopsis: Gives users the autonomy to complete different job steps simultaneously or in an unprescribed order (e.g., doing safety checks and parts checks), removing unnecessary linear restrictions that could cause inefficiency. Acceptance Criteria: Admins must be able to define steps that can be completed in parallel within the AGX Orchestration. Mobile users must be able to interact with and complete these steps in whatever order makes the most logical sense to them. Basic Testing Criteria: Set up an orchestration containing parallel steps. Access the job on a mobile device, complete the parallel steps in various sequences, and ensure that completion of the stage accurately reflects the fulfillment of all parallel steps.

epics.name: 264 [Workforce Scheduling GA] Template Enhancements
epics.description: Synopsis: Enhances the base AGX templates and creates new out-of-the-box (OOTB) templates tailored for specific industry use cases (such as Public Sector, Manufacturing, and Utilities) to accelerate time to value and reduce implementation costs. Acceptance Criteria: Base templates must be updated to include Location and Contact cards in the Confirm Job step. New OOTB templates must be provided for Safety & Compliance Inspections, Preventive/Routine Maintenance, and Break/Fix Equipment Repair. Basic Testing Criteria: Deploy the new and updated templates in a test environment. Verify that the configured cards and flows display as intended without requiring heavy custom development.

epics.name: [266][SFS Mobile Assets][Android] Notifications Priority
epics.description: Description (The "What") This epic involves implementing a tiered notification system for the AAA ACE Android application. It introduces differnet notifications priority to differentiate "Current Work" (Dispatched/In-Progress) from "Scheduled Work" and "Routine Updates." This includes different audio, unique haptic (vibration) patterns, configurable display, and the ability for technicians to opt-in to "Do Not Disturb" bypass for critical job changes. Benefits/Goals (The "Why") What customer problem does this solve? It solves Notification Fatigue . Currently, all alerts sound the same, causing technicians to ignore their phones. This leads to missed cancellations or address changes while the tech is "En-Route," resulting in wasted fuel and time. What data, customer insight, or business trend makes this feature important and timely? With a workforce of 8,000 technicians, even a small percentage of missed "Canceled" alerts represents a massive operational cost. The goal is to reduce missed critical notifications by 50% and ensure a response time of < 2 minutes for active jobs. Target Customer/Persona (The "Who") Field Technicians using Android mobile devices . Customer Outcomes / High-Level Requirements Sensory Differentiation: Technicians can identify a high-priority job update by sound and vibration alone, without looking at the screen. Critical Bypass: Users have the option to ensure critical work updates break through "Do Not Disturb" settings. User Scenarios in Scope As a technician driving to a job , I want a unique "Priority" sound to play if the job is canceled, so I can pull over safely or stop driving immediately. As a technician in a loud environment , I want a distinct vibration pattern for Dispatched jobs so I can feel the urgency even if I can't hear the phone. As a technician on a break , I want routine sync notifications to use the default sound so I am not unnecessarily interrupted. Out of Scope (i.e. Non-Goals) iOS Support: This release is strictly for the Android platform. Text-to-Speech: Read-aloud functionality for notification bodies is deferred. Logic Changes: No changes to the FSL "Drip-Feed" dispatching logic itself. Testing Hardware Diversity: Test haptic patterns across various Android device models to ensure "perceptible difference." State Testing: Verify that notifications correctly transition from "Default" to "Priority" sounds the moment a Service Appointment status changes to "Dispatched." OS Compatibility: Ensure full functionality on Android 8.0 through the latest current version. Acceptance Criteria Priority Trigger: Unique sound/haptic triggers only for Service Appointments and Work Orders in the "Dispatched" or "In-Progress" status category. Default Fallback: All other app notifications (e.g., data sync, future schedule updates) must use the system default settings. User Control: Technicians must be able to toggle sounds/haptics off via the Android System Settings for the specific app channels. Performance: Custom sounds must fire within 1 second of the notification being received by the device.

epics.name: [iOS] [SFS Mobile Assets] Migrate Record Edit XCTest suite to Swift Testing
epics.description: Migrate the Record Edit test suite in FieldService-iOS from XCTest (XCTestCase / XCTAssert / setUpWithError) to the Swift Testing framework (import Testing / @Suite struct / @Test / #expect / #require), matching the pattern already adopted across ~100 files in the repo (e.g. WorkPlansListDataControllerTests, WorkPlans* suites). Scope: ~24 XCTest files under FieldServiceSDK/FieldServiceUITests/Classes/RecordEdit, plus FieldServiceSDK/FieldServiceSDKTests/Integration/Features/RecordEdit/RecordFormViewModelIntegrationTests.swift. LookupViewModelManagingTests.swift (SDKTests/Features/RecordEdit) is ALREADY on Swift Testing and is excluded. Broken into small per-file stories (with the 5,596-line RecordFormViewModelTests split into sub-stories by concern). Why: Swift Testing is the repo's standard going forward. Consolidating the Record Edit suite improves readability (#expect vs XCTAssert), enables parameterized tests and .tags/.serialized traits, removes Optional force-unwrap in setUp via TestContext.make(), and keeps the suite consistent with the rest of the codebase. Migration conventions (from existing migrated suites): - Replace `final class XTests: XCTestCase` with `@Suite("...", .tags(.recordEdit), .serialized) struct XTests` (add @MainActor where UI/main-actor bound). - Replace setUpWithError/tearDownWithError instance state with a `TestContext` struct + `static func make()` factory; construct per-test. - Replace XCTAssert* with #expect(...) and force-unwraps with try #require(...). - Replace XCTestExpectation/wait with async/await or confirmation { }. - Preserve Cuckoo / OCMockitoSwift / Hamcrest usage; keep test intent and coverage identical. Acceptance for the epic: all in-scope files migrated, no remaining `import XCTest` / `XCTestCase` in the RecordEdit test folders, full RecordEdit suite passes on CI, no loss of test coverage.

epics.name: 264 - SFS Mobile - C&S - Test automation
epics.description: Epic to cover C&S test automation enhancements. Goal: Work order overview screen automated with Key Q3 tests. Timeboxed 1 sprint per platform. Test plans for all comms and search tests cleaned up and improved. Estimated to remove bad tests and ensure steps are documented for AI. Estimated one developer sprint. Total:25 WOO Test Automation — Work Items (W-22162465) Detailed, reviewable, GUS-format work-item descriptions decomposing the spike W-22162465 [Spike] Test Automation Plan for Automation of WOO Tests , under Epic 264 — SFS Mobile - C&S - Test automation (a3QEE000002KnrR2AS). These are drafts for review with [reviewer]. After sign-off they become GUS work items (User Stories) under Epic 264. Each description follows the GUS user-story format (User Story → Background → Acceptance Criteria → Automation Approach → Assets → Dependencies → DoD → Cross-cutting/DoR → Estimate & Owner) and is written to be Claude-executable . The work items WI Work Item Title Auto Depends on Gates WI-1 W-23157720 Export & triage the 179 P0–P2 WOO scenarios (prune obsolete/duplicate) High — WI-2, WI-4 WI-2 W-23157729 Cross-reference scenarios vs existing iOS/Android tests; mark already-covered Automated High WI-1 WI-4, WI-7 WI-3 W-23157736 Q2 view-model coverage audit (iOS dashboard + Android equiv) High — (parallel) WI-4 WI-4 W-23157744 Classify remaining scenarios → Q1/Q2/must-be-Q3, naming target code Med WI-2, WI-3 WI-5, WI-6 WI-5 W-23157753 Design the 3–5 Maestro parent flows for the WOO seam Low (human) WI-4 WI-7 WI-6 W-23157811 Author Q1/Q2 tests for push-down candidates; mark automated Med WI-4 — WI-7 W-23157817 Author Maestro flows; re-automate legacy 27; obsolete superseded Med WI-5, WI-2 — WI-8 W-23157823 Review checkpoint with [reviewer] to validate strategy + samples Low (human gate) WI-1..WI-5 WI-6, WI-7, bulk writes Suggested sequence: WI-1 → (WI-2 ∥ WI-3) → WI-4 → WI-5 → WI-8 sign-off → (WI-6 ∥ WI-7). Assets All produced/consumed data files are attached to this epic as woo-assets.zip . The only file with real data today is WI-1_woo_p0-p2_scenarios.csv (the live 179-scenario export) and its WI-1_scenarios_with_ids.csv (179/179 record Ids resolved). Every other CSV/doc is a header-only / outline stub that the corresponding WI fills when it executes — the exact column headers and generating sf queries are specified in each WI's Assets section. How the drafts were produced Authored by a sequential agent pipeline: each WI was written on top of all accepted prior WIs, then a reviewer agent checked it against its predecessor for dependency/requirement consistency, sending a prior WI back for re-authoring when it found a breaking gap. WI-1..WI-7 completed this loop; WI-8 was authored directly in the same format. Ground truth (the 179-record export, the ADM_Test_Scenario__c field model, seam discipline, GUS/DoR format) was pinned for every agent so nothing was re-derived unreliably. Work item walkthrough (for review) The plan turns a large, manually-run Work Order Overview regression suite into a small set of automated tests. We start from 179 priority (P0–P2) test scenarios and move each one to the cheapest place it can live: delete the dead ones, recognize the ones already covered by code, push what we can down to fast developer tests, and reserve a handful of full end-to-end tests for the journeys that truly need them. The eight work items below are that journey, in order. The first five are analysis and design; a review gate sits in the middle; the last two are the actual test-building. Most of the analysis work is automatable — Claude does the heavy lifting and a human approves before anything is changed for real. WI-1 — Clean up the test list. Produce one agreed, de-duplicated, pruned working set of the 179 scenarios so every later step builds on the same clean foundation. Obsolete tests are flagged (they can't be deleted, only retired) and near-duplicates are grouped for a merge decision. Output: a reviewed triage worksheet. WI-2 — Find what we already test. Cross-reference each surviving scenario against the existing iOS and Android code, so anything already verified by a real, current test is marked "automated" with the exact covering test recorded. Output: a coverage map. WI-3 — Measure mid-level coverage. Run an automated, repeatable audit of which Work Order Overview screens already have "Q2" (developer integration) test coverage, so the next step starts from facts rather than guesses about where the real gaps are. Output: a coverage gap list. WI-4 — Decide where each test belongs. Classify every remaining scenario into the lowest, cheapest test level that can still prove it — naming the specific piece of code each test should target — so the build steps get an unambiguous to-do list. Output: a per-scenario build list. WI-5 — Design the end-to-end tests. Consolidate the scenarios that genuinely need full end-to-end coverage into just 3–5 "parent" flows , each a realistic customer journey through the overview screen. This is the key design judgment (and the natural point to review with the senior QE). Output: flow designs. WI-6 — Build the fast tests. Turn WI-4's push-down candidates into real, merged, passing unit/integration tests on each platform, and only mark a scenario "automated" in the system after its test is actually merged. Output: merged tests + updated records. WI-7 — Build the end-to-end tests. Implement WI-5's flow designs as real, passing automated UI tests (Maestro) that run in our nightly pipeline, re-build the ~27 tests still running on the old framework, and retire the individual scenarios each new flow replaces — again, only once the test is merged and green. This is the largest item and a candidate to split by platform. Output: merged end-to-end flows + updated records. WI-8 — The sign-off gate. A single checkpoint where the senior QE ([reviewer]) reviews and approves the cleanup, coverage, classification, and flow design from WI-1–WI-5 before any records are changed in bulk or any test-building begins. Nothing irreversible happens until this sign-off is recorded. Output: a review packet + recorded approval.

Core: Emergency-Dispatch Notification tier signal (264, Android + iOS)
epics.description: When a Service Appointment with IsEmergency = true is dispatched, Core delivers that dispatch notification at the Emergency tier (one of three fixed tiers: Standard / High / Emergency) so the mobile app renders it with emergency treatment. In 264 Core produces only the Standard and Emergency tiers, on both Android (FCM) and iOS (APNS). MECHANISM — RE-TIER, NOT A SECOND NOTIFICATION. Core keeps emitting the same dispatch notification and resolves its tier to Emergency when the gate below is true; it does not send a second push and suppress the first. This satisfies "one notification, not two — never flash the standard first" for free, because only one notification is ever produced. Core signals the tier in the push payload; the app renders the alert (sound/haptics/visual are app-owned — see cross-team dependency). PLATFORM-NEUTRAL CONTRACT. The tier is carried as sfdc.tier in the push payload, which already serves both FCM (Android) and APNS (iOS) — so the tier signal, the trigger gate, and per-recipient resolution are single-implementation and cover both platforms. The only platform-specific piece is the transport-priority gate: FCM high-priority on Android and its APNS equivalent (interruption level / priority) on iOS, both gated on the Emergency tier. TRIGGER GATE (resolved per recipient, in the async delivery handler, off the Service Appointment the message already carries): new Emergency-Dispatch setting = ON (read against the RECIPIENT's profile) AND ServiceAppointment.IsEmergency = true AND ServiceAppointment is (or was) Dispatched AND the event is a resource ASSIGNMENT (ENTITY_CREATED), not an un-assignment -> resolve tier = EMERGENCY (else STANDARD) The Emergency alert is INDEPENDENT of the standard dispatch-notification setting (IsDispatchNotification): it fires even when the technician has routine dispatch notifications turned off. It is gated only by its own new opt-in setting, which is DEFAULT OFF — so the feature is strictly additive and nothing changes on upgrade until an admin enables it per profile. Tier is resolved once in the delivery handler (producer-agnostic, FLS-safe, nothing carried across the async boundary) and carried to the device as sfdc.tier; the Emergency tier sets high transport priority (FCM high on Android, the APNS equivalent on iOS) so the device wakes promptly. CORE SCOPE (264): new per-profile admin setting (default OFF); enqueue emergency candidates past both dispatch-producer drop-gates; resolve the tier per recipient in the delivery handler and bridge it onto the notification; carry the tier onto the push payload (FCM + APNS) and gate high-priority on Emergency on both transports. DESIGN CONTRACTS: - Emergency tier is resolved at DISPATCH TIME ONLY. A later change to IsEmergency on an already-dispatched appointment does not retroactively fire or downgrade the alert. - Un-assigning a resource from an emergency appointment stays Standard. - Multi-recipient dispatch is evaluated per recipient against each recipient's own profile; a crew recipient receives the Standard notification and is never dropped. - Fail-open: if the IsEmergency read is ever inconclusive, resolve toward sending the alert. EXPLICITLY NOT IN THIS EPIC: app-side rendering (see cross-team dependency); any Emergency-sound override (MDM or core-upload) — 264 ships the app's bundled default sound only; the High tier producer; per-notification telemetry / per-org "Emergency sent" count. CROSS-TEAM DEPENDENCY (parallel 264 workstream): app-side rendering on both platforms — sound, haptics, DND/Focus breakthrough, iOS Time-Sensitive interruption-level handling, visual tier marker — is FS Mobile app-team-owned and also targeted for 264 (both iOS and Android, per Sandeep). It consumes this epic's sfdc.tier contract; sequence so the core contract lands in time for the app teams to build against it. FORWARD-COMPAT (not a 264 blocker): the tier contract Core establishes here (getNotificationTier() + sfdc.tier, three tiers) should be reused by Mobile Core Services / UNS (TD-0319603) rather than a parallel path. Confirm before 266 planning. --- SOURCE: spike W-22914294 (Emergency Pulse Channel); PRD 264-notification-priority-prd.md (FR-001, FR-003, FR-005, FR-005a, FR-008). Associate with TD-0319625; link under parent epic Priority Notifications (a3QEE000002KmKH2A0). --- SUCCESS CRITERIA: 1. With the Emergency setting ON for the recipient's profile and an emergency Service Appointment dispatched, exactly one notification is delivered at the Emergency tier on both Android and iOS; the standard dispatch notification is never separately sent or visibly flashed first. 2. The Emergency alert fires even when the recipient's standard dispatch-notification setting is OFF (independent of IsDispatchNotification). 3. With the Emergency setting OFF (default), behavior is unchanged from today for every notification (strictly additive). 4. Tier is resolved at dispatch time only; a post-dispatch change to IsEmergency does not retroactively fire or downgrade the alert. 5. Un-assigning a resource from an emergency appointment does not fire at the Emergency tier. 6. Assign-then-dispatch of an emergency appointment in one transaction yields exactly one Emergency notification, not two (verified by functional test). 7. The resolved tier is carried as sfdc.tier in both the FCM and APNS payloads; the Emergency tier sets high transport priority on both. 8. Each recipient on a multi-recipient dispatch is evaluated independently; a crew recipient receives the Standard notification and is never dropped.

epics.name: 266 SFS Mobile - [AA] Migrate Google Maps Directions/Matrix to Routes API
epics.description: Migrate Appointment Assistant's usage of the Google Maps Platform legacy Directions API and Distance Matrix API to the newer Routes API and Routes Matrix API. BACKGROUND Google Maps Platform is sunsetting the legacy Directions & Distance Matrix APIs in favor of the re-architected Routes & Routes Matrix APIs. Per the migration doc, Appointment Assistant and the SFS Android app are the two identified consumers of the legacy APIs. - Formal Deprecation: H1 2026 (legacy APIs move to Maintenance Mode - P0 bug fixes only, no new features). - Service Degradation: H1 2027 (earliest). - Full Discontinuation: 2028 or later (legacy APIs no longer callable). Google is actively pushing customers to migrate ahead of these dates. SCOPE (Appointment Assistant) - Inventory all AA calls to the Directions and Distance Matrix APIs. - Implement the Routes API / Routes Matrix API behind a feature flag in a Beta build; keep legacy API in production during a trial period and compare results. - Implement field masking (request only needed fields, e.g. routes.duration, routes.distanceMeters) to optimize payload size, performance, and cost. - Gradually cut over traffic to the Routes API, starting with lower-priority flows. RELATED WORK - Android equivalent: W-21809401 '[Android] Replace Google Maps API' (User Story, team SFS Mobile Location and DC, tag 'SFS - Mobile - Maps', under epic '266 SFS Mobile - [Trust] SFS Planned Trust Enhancements'). - Product tag for AA child stories: 'SFS Mobile App - Appointment Assistant' REFERENCES - Migration doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1wOPO_ZtWV2yEYJ8iNHrPlppAuyiVnv0Z5huJ8HpxWBI/edit - Why migrate: https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/routes/migrate-routes-why - How to migrate (technical): https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/routes/migrate-routes - Google POC: Jon Fusco - AA POC: Adi Sharet

epics.name: 264 SFS Mobile Platform DX - Swift 6 Migration
epics.description: Migrate FieldService-iOS to Swift 6 / strict concurrency, target-by-target, with a CI ratchet that prevents regressions. Consolidated tracking epic for all 6 sub-epics (to be split out later). Phases / sub-epics: 1. Groundwork & Guardrails (Phase 0, Low) — Danger concurrency ratchet, ~12 zero-risk var→let fixes, SwiftFormat 6 bump, measurement recipe. 2. Pilot — Independent Targets (Phase 1, Low) — SFSWidget + UI pods to Swift 6. 3. Dependencies DI Inversion (Phase 2, High, XL) — CRITICAL PATH; break the 449-line god object so lower layers stop referencing concrete UI Dependencies. 4. Racy Singletons & GCD (Phase 2-3, Med) — 6 racy singletons, 56 .sync sites. 5. Delegates & Callbacks (Phase 2-3, Med) — 62 delegate protocols, 259 prod @escaping (~150-170 cross isolation). 6. Framework Burn-Down & Flip (Phase 2-4, High, XL) — strict-concurrency warnings to zero, flip SWIFT_VERSION=6. Critical path = Dependencies DI inversion. Cross-cutting constraints: flag via xcconfig only (command-line leaks into Pods and crashes the compiler); pod sync required before builds; Danger PR-size gate hard-fails at 2000 lines; React Native out of scope. Headline measured numbers (Xcode 26.2 / Swift 6.2.3, static analysis 2026-06-09): ~781 framework warnings + 3 hard errors; 6 racy singletons; 259 production @escaping across 127 files; 62 delegate protocols (0 isolated); 56 DispatchQueue.sync sites. Readiness ~6.5/10. Source docs: swift6-migration-plan.md, swift6-spike.md, swift6-epics/ (6 problem statements).

epics.name: [266 Atlas] TDs and Trust
[266] Drag and Drop Shifts on the Grid
epics.description: Use drag and drop actions on the grid to move shifts PRD - https://docs.google.com/document/d/1nLbkSOuf8Cx6Jk9zR3cD8iBkFv_zQLexGNqVCiB67YI/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.wiklgl6fia8k UX Link - https://shiftmanager-262-scope-ca916c26db1e.herokuapp.com/ Drag and Drop Shift Templates Capability The Problem: Managers and shift planners often spend hours manually typing out shift details—such as start times, end times, roles, and break durations—for every single employee on a weekly or monthly schedule. This repetitive, manual data entry is incredibly tedious and highly prone to human error. A simple typo can result in understaffing, overlapping shifts, or an employee showing up at the wrong time, which ultimately impacts business operations and employee satisfaction. The Solution: Introduce a sidebar or menu of pre-configured shift templates (e.g., "Morning Cashier: 8 AM - 4 PM" or "Night Shift: 10 PM - 6 AM") alongside the main calendar grid. Users can simply click on a specific template, drag it across the screen, and drop it directly into the desired cell (representing an employee and a specific date) on the scheduling grid to instantly assign that exact shift. User Story - As a schedule manager, I want to drag and drop pre-configured shift templates directly onto specific employee rows and date columns within the scheduling grid, So that I can build accurate schedules faster, eliminate manual typing errors, and visually confirm coverage in real-time. Acceptance Criteria: Template Availability & Drag Initiation Given the user is viewing the scheduling grid When they look at the template sidebar/menu Then they should see a list of pre-configured shift templates And clicking and holding a template should immediately pick it up and attach a visual representation of the shift to the cursor. 2. Visual Feedback During Drag (Hover State) Given the user is dragging a shift template across the screen When the cursor hovers over a valid cell (intersecting an employee row and a date column) on the scheduling grid Then the targeted cell should highlight or visually indicate that it is ready to receive the drop. 3. Successful Drop & Assignment Given the user is hovering a dragged template over a valid grid cell When the user releases the mouse button (drops the template) Then a new shift block matching the template's details (start time, end time, role) should instantly appear in that cell And the shift should be automatically assigned to the corresponding employee on that specific date And the schedule data should save automatically. 4. Invalid Drop Location Given the user is dragging a shift template When the user releases the mouse button outside of a valid scheduling grid cell (e.g., on the navigation bar or empty space) Then the template should visually snap back to its origin in the sidebar And no new shift should be created on the schedule. 5. Handling Pre-existing Shifts (Conflict) Given a user drags a template over a cell that already contains a scheduled shift When the user drops the template Then the system should either add the new shift alongside the existing one (if multiple shifts per day are allowed) or display a prompt warning the user of a shift conflict.

epics.name: [266] Rule Violations and Alerts
[266] Shift Rotation
epics.description: Contact center schedulers need a way to define a repeating shift rotation pattern (e.g., Morning → Afternoon → Night) and assign agents to it, so that when a roster is generated for any date range, each agent is automatically placed on the correct shift based on where they are in the rotation cycle, without the scheduler having to manually track or calculate individual agent positions. HLD - https://docs.google.com/document/d/14w6oSdvGcogCaTd5UFyg6bqKiD5aWrWjIjvbkytjPNg/edit?tab=t.0 Product Vision A scheduler generates shifts from a repeating pattern and gets them filled, on demand, for any date range, without hand-building each schedule or babysitting a background job. Problem Today there is no clean way to (1) fill pattern-generated shifts automatically under a chosen policy (2) rotate resources through shift classes over time so no one is stuck on let’s say nights, or (3) reuse a hand-built roster across date ranges. Solution Manual and Automatic resource-selection modes from a single Rotation Builder.

epics.name: [268 Atlas] TDs and Trust
Auto Refresh of Gantt
epics.description: To ensure that planners and schedule managers viewing the Gantt chart always see the most up-to-date schedule. The Gantt UI must automatically refresh without manual user intervention when relevant scheduling records are created, updated, or deleted in the background. The Gantt chart must listen for and react to background database changes (Create, Update, Delete) on the following objects: Service Appointment, Service Resource, Shift, Resource Absence, Service Territory Member, Job Profile. The UI should only refresh or re-render records if the background change belongs to the current filtering criteria. (date/time, field filters) Changes outside the user's current view should be ignored to save processing power and bandwidth. The refresh must not interrupt a planner who is actively dragging/dropping/updating a record or editing a modal. If a background update modifies a record currently visible on the screen, a brief visual indicator (e.g., a subtle highlight or flash) should denote that the record has been updated. NFR: The auto-refresh listener must not degrade the initial load time of the Gantt chart.

epics.name: Quick Filter Accordion
epics.description: The EPIC focuses on adding search and filter capabilities on the coverage grid. PRD - https://docs.google.com/document/d/1TM5AZoHXifT2ioIeAOaeS17ufcnpDE-ZhGURoYWYfqc/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.wiklgl6fia8k UX Link - https://shiftmanager-262-scope-ca916c26db1e.herokuapp.com/ Advanced Filters and Search Capability The Problem: Schedulers often struggle to isolate relevant data amidst thousands of shift records. Finding specific skills, rule violations, or coverage gaps requires navigating multiple screens or scrolling endlessly. The Solution: A granular filtering allowing multi-select criteria such as Service Territory, Job Profile, Skills, Custom Objects, Request Types, Violations, Status, Shift Template combined with a "Smart Object Search" helps narrow down the results for effective review and updates. User Story: As a Planner When I am viewing a schedule board populated with hundreds of shifts and resources. I want to instantly isolate specific subsets of data (e.g., finding all Electricians in NY or finding a specific employee by name). So that I can focus on relevant information and make targeted updates without scrolling through irrelevant data. Acceptance Criteria - P0. Ability to save and retrieve filters: Users should be able to save the filters they create and easily retrieve them. they should also be able to persist their filter as default filter everytime they load the shift ui. They should also be able to provide a name to their filters eg. team 1 etc. 1. UI & Filter Accessibility Scenario: Accessing the filtering interface Given the user is viewing the schedule or shift list, When they click the "Filter" icon or expand the filter panel, Then they are presented with a "Smart Object Search" bar at the top. And they see collapsible/expandable sections for granular multi-select filters: Service Territory, Service Resource, Job Profile, Skills, Custom Objects, Request Types, and Violations. 2. Multi-Select Filtering Logic Scenario: Selecting criteria within the same category (OR logic) Given the user is using the granular filters, When they select multiple options within the same category (e.g., selecting both "Dispatcher" and "Technician" under Job Profile), Then the results update to show shifts/resources matching any of the selected options (Job Profile = Dispatcher OR Technician). Scenario: Selecting criteria across different categories (AND logic) Given the user is using the granular filters, When they select options across different categories (e.g., Service Territory = "North Region" AND Skills = "Electrical"), Then the results update to show only shifts/resources that match all the selected cross-category criteria. Scenario: Filtering by Request Types and Violations Given the user is managing exceptions on the schedule, When they filter by "Request Types" (e.g., PTO, Shift Swap), Then the view filters to display only resources or shifts that have pending or approved requests of those types. When they filter by "Violations" (e.g., Overtime, Rest Period Violation), Then the view highlights and isolates shifts or schedules currently triggering those specific rule violations. 3. Smart Object Search Logic Scenario: Using the Smart Object Search Given the user is looking for a specific record or keyword, When they type text into the "Smart Object Search" bar (e.g., a resource's name, a specific shift ID, or a custom object reference), Then the system dynamically searches across all indexed fields and related objects on the schedule. And the results instantly narrow down to display only the schedules, resources, or shifts containing that text string. Scenario: Combining Smart Search with Granular Filters Given the user has applied multi-select filters (e.g., Territory = "East"), When they type a keyword into the "Smart Object Search", Then the search string is applied only to the currently filtered dataset, further narrowing down the results. 4. Custom Objects Support Scenario: Filtering by Custom Objects Given the user's organizational setup includes custom objects tied to shifts or resources (e.g., "Vehicle Type" or "Project Code"), When they open the filter panel, Then these custom objects appear as selectable filter categories dynamically based on the system configuration. 5. Managing Filters Scenario: Clearing filters and search Given the user has applied multiple filters and a Smart Object Search string, When they click the "Clear All" or "Reset" button, Then all checkboxes are cleared, the search bar is emptied, and the schedule view returns to its default, unfiltered state. And the user can remove individual filter tags by clicking an 'x' next to the applied filter pill without clearing the entire board.

epics.name: 264 SFS [Trust] Feature Toggle Cleanup
epics.description: 264 SFS [Trust] Feature Toggle Cleanup Dedicated epic for the 264-cycle feature toggle cleanup effort — carry-over from W-21962794 ( * [262][Trust][Scheduling Intelligence] , Closed). Spawned from the FT plan documented in docs/LLM/o2-workspace/docs/LLM/264/ft/README.md . Author: Guy Eden · Owner: Yonatan Bar-Yehuda · Quality: Irad Ben Dosa One-sentence summary We are simplifying version-gated feature toggles in the O2 stack by agreeing on MpVersion 258.0.0 as the floor for production traffic, which lets us delete roughly two-thirds of the toggle predicates and remove the matching if (FT.isEnabled()) branches from 5 Java repos. Why it matters Reduced complexity. Every FT predicate is a live branch in production. 25 of them have been effectively always-on for ~6 months and are now dead weight. Deleting them cuts regression-surface area in the request and response translators. Clearer version contract. MpVersion and CoreApiVersion flow from the caller as HTTP headers → RequestContextDTO (app-infra) → MDC → FeatureToggle.isFeatureEnabled(...) . Each service parses them independently; the MpVersion ↔ CoreApiVersion mapping lives in the external FT service, not in O2 source. Fewer predicates means fewer places where a mismatch can produce a silent misfire. Unblocks v262+ work. Features gated FROM 262.0.0 ( ExcludeArrivalWindowRulesForReshuffle , ScheduleOperationRemoveTasksFromGanttBug ) need a matching CoreApiVersion(67) predicate added. Doing that while the table is still cluttered with stale 238.3 / 240.x / 244 gates was not defensible. Phases — what's done, what's in flight, what's planned Done in 262 ( W-21962794 , Closed) Existing-status enumeration: 39 features × 4 prod regions, predicates documented per region. Splunk validation that production traffic is at MpVersion ≥ 258.0.0 across all 4 regions. Automation scripts: utils/promote_to_enable.py (Playwright-driven 25-feature × 4-region console flip with backup JSON) and utils/backout_to_custom.py (revert tool with dry-run-by-default). Pre-flip JSON dumps of all 4 prod regions ( jsons/ft_prod{1,3,4,8}_*.json ). FeatureToggleConfig.json 258-floor sweep — landed in common #3132 . In flight (4 PRs, console-flip side) | Repo | PR | Scope | |---|---|---| | o2service-common | #3132 | ABRequiredTimeZoneParam, TerritoryOptimizationRequestNewFields, ReadonlyFSLEndpoint, ComplexWorkAdvanced header, FeatureToggleConfig.json 258-floor | | o2-data-translator-service | #969 | 10 Easy features: ScheduleMode, ComplexWorkSlidingOverLunchBreak, CustomerLabelsParametersEnhancement, KeepScheduledServices, OffsetInSeconds, EnableReshuffleOnScheduleAndAB, ABRequiredTimeZoneParam, AllowOvertimeImprovements, AllowOvertimeInMiddleOfShift, PreferGPUEngine | | o2-fetch-data-service | #421 | ComplexWorkAdvanced, ParallelMSW | | o2service | #3126 | FillResourceGapsRequest, KeepScheduledServices (svc side) | To-do — 10 carry-over child stories under THIS epic Total story points: 23 (≈ XL T-shirt for the FT cleanup portion). Sequencing rules Console flips before code cleanup. Removing a source-side branch first would force the enabled path for any sub-258 client. 5-day observation window between flipping the console in all 4 regions and merging the per-feature code-cleanup PRs. Hard features ( ResourceContinuousAvailability , SALifeCycle ) get dedicated PRs with human integration testing. Yaml model regen runs only after the matching if (FT.isEnabled()) branches are gone. Operational artifacts Forward script: python docs/LLM/264/ft/utils/promote_to_enable.py --env prod{1,3,4,8} — 25-feature × 1-region console flip per run. Back-out script (immediate): python docs/LLM/264/ft/utils/backout_to_custom.py --env prod1 --apply . Recommended sequencing: dev4 → perf1 → test1 → (observe) → prod1 → prod3 → prod4 → prod8 . Stakeholders Implementor: Guy Eden Validator: Yonatan Bar-Yehuda QA Engineer: Irad Ben Dosa Approver / Code review: Orelie Fridler + team

epics.description: As an Android field technician working in environments where my hands are occupied or conditions are unsafe for device interaction, I want to access Pre-Work Briefs, ask follow-up questions, and complete key workflow steps using fully hands-free voice interactions, so that I can stay productive, reduce task switching, and complete jobs more safely and efficiently. Allow technicians to ask conversational follow-up questions without touching the device. Ensure performance and accuracy on commonly used Android devices in field environments (noise, gloves, limited visibility). Maintain compliance with safety, privacy, and offline/low-connectivity requirements as needed. Success Metrics ↓ Reduction in task-switching time during field service workflows. ↑ Increase in PWB usage and follow-up question frequency. ↑ Technician CSAT/NPS for usability and safety. Demonstrated reliability across major Android hardware configurations. Dependencies Agentforce SDK for two-way voice. Pre-Work Brief context and follow-up question integration.

epics.name: 266 SFS Frontline AI - Core Trust
266 SFS Frontline AI - Feature Architecture (AI-Ready Source of Truth)
epics.description: 🎯 Objective The goal of this epic is to create a comprehensive, highly structured wiki page documenting the architecture, data flow, and design patterns of the [Feature Name] feature. This documentation is explicitly intended to serve as a high-fidelity context injection for LLMs and AI coding assistants. When fed this document, an AI should be able to accurately locate bugs, reason about state, and generate new code that strictly adheres to our established architectural patterns without drifting. 📋 Scope of Work & Requirements To ensure the wiki page is "AI-readable," it must avoid vague summaries and instead focus on strict technical specifications. The wiki page created under this epic must include: 1. System Overview & Component Boundaries A clear breakdown of where this feature lives in the codebase. Explicit definitions of the boundaries between components (e.g., UI Layer -> State Management -> API Service). Requirement: List the exact file paths or directory structures relevant to this feature. 2. Detailed Data Flow & State Management A step-by-step lifecycle of data (e.g., how a user action triggers an API call, how the response is parsed, and how the state is updated). Deterministic state diagrams or text-based sequence descriptions that AI can easily parse. 3. Strict Code Patterns & Idioms Document the specific design patterns used (e.g., Repository pattern, Factory pattern, Hook-based state). Anti-patterns: A dedicated section explicitly stating what not to do (e.g., "Do not bypass the service layer to call the database directly from the component" ). AI learns incredibly well from negative constraints. 4. 266 SFS Frontline AI - NGA agent_router Routing Reliability
epics.description: Description — Target Customer and Benefit / Goal The Field Mobile Worker agent on NGA (New Agentforce Builder) ships three team-owned subagents wired to a single agent_router : TroubleshootingForMobileWorker , PostWorkSummary , and InteractivePreWorkBriefForFieldService . In production we observe intermittent misrouting — the router transitions to the wrong subagent, particularly when subagent instructions/descriptions overlap. Source-level review of chatbots/module-graph-runtime ( RouterNode / FlashClassifier ) confirmed the headline finding : the router's reasoning.instructions block does not enter the classifier call. Routing is a tool-call where the LLM sees exactly one string per subagent — NodeReference.description . Overlap in those descriptions is the direct cause of misroutes; no prose added to router-level reasoning.instructions can fix it. This epic delivers the concrete authoring + platform changes that actually move the needle: (1) rewrite the three team-owned subagent descriptions using the PostWorkSummary structure as a template, (2) add available when guards to go_to_* transitions using existing page-context and a new WorkOrderStatus variable, (3) pin the router to sfdc_ai__DefaultEinsteinHyperClassifier , and (4) run an eight-utterance evaluation suite covering the ambiguity zones. Source document: W-22860883 — NGA agent_router Routing Reliability Exploration (local copy: ~/Documents/claude/W-22860883-router-exploration.md ). Parent work item: W-22860883 . Acceptance Criteria Three team-owned subagent descriptions rewritten to follow PostWorkSummary structure: name the audience (field worker), the entity (work order / product / asset), the lifecycle stage (pre-arrival / in-progress / completed), 3+ positive utterance examples, explicit "Do NOT use" section referencing sibling subagents. available when guards added to go_to_InteractivePreWorkBriefForFieldService , go_to_TroubleshootingForMobileWorker , and go_to_PostWorkSummary transitions on the router. Router model_config.model pinned to sfdc_ai__DefaultEinsteinHyperClassifier (currently unset — falls back to org-default reasoner). Eight-utterance evaluation suite (§7 of the source doc) passes on the updated agent, measured either via sfdc.co/agentscript-dev live editor or a scratch-org deploy. ROUTER_CLASSIFIER_CHOICES span attribute is observable in Splunk/Argus for post-deploy verification in prod. Legacy Agent Builder Classic path continues to work (regression parity) — verified via W-22933766 Suite 2. Known Dependencies / Risks Dependency — sfdc_fieldservice__FieldServiceMobileWork template ownership. The description rewrites modify the template itself. Confirm sole SFS Frontline AI ownership vs. shared with other cloud teams (Niv Garber / #nga-template-migration ). Dependency — WorkOrderStatus variable population. Path 2 available when guards require a new agent variable populated via before_reasoning_iteration reading WorkOrder.Status off currentRecordId . Product-level decision required. Dependency — observability access. ROUTER_CLASSIFIER_CHOICES span attribute visibility in prod Splunk/Argus (Olivier Martin / Nico Pappagianis). Risk — customer-authored neighboring subagents. Org-specific subagents next to ours cannot be enumerated in advance. Description rewrites defend by naming entity + lifecycle stage explicitly (§4.2 of source doc). Risk — currentObjectApiName may be blank in messaging-only sessions. Path 1 weak guards silently disappear subagents if the variable is unset. Verify populate-timing before adopting. Out of Scope Legacy Topic Selector / SOMA path — not in scope; the router covered here is NGA RouterNode only. additional_parameter__enable_serial_tool_state_chaining (Lever H) — not source-confirmed; deferred pending Stefan Krawczyk clarification. Router-level reasoning.instructions rewrite (Lever F) — confirmed no-op per §3.3 of source doc. Customer-authored subagent audits — customer orgs own their own subagents. Definition of Done PO has accepted the epic All child WIs closed and their ACs met Description rewrites reviewed with template co-owners Eight-utterance eval suite green on the updated agent ROUTER_CLASSIFIER_CHOICES span visible in prod for post-deploy monitoring Regression: Classic path preview (W-22933766 Suite 2) still passes Resources Source exploration doc: W-22860883 router exploration Parent WI: W-22860883 Runtime engine: chatbots/module-graph-runtime ( RouterNode , FlashClassifier ) Compiler: chatbots/agent-dsl Sibling implementation reference: FieldService Scheduling Agent on NGA (Niv Garber, June 2026) Support channels: #agentscript-dev , #technical-support-new-agent-builder-and-script

266 SFS Frontline AI - [Android] Merge Offline Voice to Form into main branch
epics.description: Voice to Form (V2F) offline is built as a pilot in a separate feature branch. As on-device models improve, mid- and high-tier device penetration grows in the FSL install base, and pilot usage signals demand, we see a path to GA'ing offline V2F. To de-risk that path and unblock parallel work on master, we will merge the offline V2F feature branch back into master and keep the functionality behind a feature flag (off by default). This protects existing V2F online behavior for all customers while allowing the pilot cohort — and future GA rollout — to be controlled via flag/entitlement without maintaining a long-lived divergent branch. In scope: - Rebase and merge the offline V2F feature branch into master; resolve conflicts. - Wrap all offline V2F entry points, model loading, and offline sync paths behind a feature flag (default OFF for all orgs). - Ensure zero behavior change for online V2F when the flag is OFF. - Update CI so offline V2F unit + integration tests run on master. - Migrate any pilot-specific config/telemetry to flag-gated code paths. - Documentation: internal enablement notes for the flag and how to toggle for pilots. Out of scope: - Enabling the flag for any production org (handled via separate LAP/enablement work). - Model updates, UX enhancements, or new-language support (tracked under separate epics). - Public documentation / release notes (deferred until GA epic). Success criteria: - Feature branch fully merged into master with zero unresolved conflicts. - CI green on master post-merge across unit, integration, and offline sync test suites. - Flag OFF: online V2F behavior byte-for-byte identical to pre-merge master (verified by regression pass). - Flag ON in a pilot org: offline V2F end-to-end scenario passes (record → offline → sync). - No open P0/P1 regressions attributable to the merge two weeks post-merge. - Feature branch retired; all downstream offline V2F stories rebase on master.

epics.description: Voice to Form (V2F) offline is built as a pilot in a separate feature branch. As on-device models improve, mid- and high-tier device penetration grows in the FSL install base, and pilot usage signals demand, we see a path to GA'ing offline V2F. To de-risk that path and unblock parallel work on master, we will merge the offline V2F feature branch back into master and keep the functionality behind a feature flag (off by default). This protects existing V2F online behavior for all customers while allowing the pilot cohort — and future GA rollout — to be controlled via flag/entitlement without maintaining a long-lived divergent branch. In scope: - Rebase and merge the offline V2F feature branch into master; resolve conflicts. - Wrap all offline V2F entry points, model loading, and offline sync paths behind a feature flag (default OFF for all orgs). - Ensure zero behavior change for online V2F when the flag is OFF. - Update CI so offline V2F unit + integration tests run on master. - Migrate any pilot-specific config/telemetry to flag-gated code paths. - Documentation: internal enablement notes for the flag and how to toggle for pilots. Out of scope: - Enabling the flag for any production org (handled via separate LAP/enablement work). - Model updates, UX enhancements, or new-language support (tracked under separate epics). - Public documentation / release notes (deferred until GA epic). Success criteria: - Feature branch fully merged into master with zero unresolved conflicts. - CI green on master post-merge across unit, integration, and offline sync test suites. - Flag OFF: online V2F behavior byte-for-byte identical to pre-merge master (verified by regression pass). - Flag ON in a pilot org: offline V2F end-to-end scenario passes (record → offline → sync). - No open P0/P1 regressions attributable to the merge two weeks post-merge. - Feature branch retired; all downstream offline V2F stories rebase on master.

[266][SFS Mobile Assets][Android] Notifications Priority
epics.description: Description (The "What") This epic involves implementing a tiered notification system for the AAA ACE Android application. It introduces differnet notifications priority to differentiate "Current Work" (Dispatched/In-Progress) from "Scheduled Work" and "Routine Updates." This includes different audio, unique haptic (vibration) patterns, configurable display, and the ability for technicians to opt-in to "Do Not Disturb" bypass for critical job changes. Benefits/Goals (The "Why") What customer problem does this solve? It solves Notification Fatigue . Currently, all alerts sound the same, causing technicians to ignore their phones. This leads to missed cancellations or address changes while the tech is "En-Route," resulting in wasted fuel and time. What data, customer insight, or business trend makes this feature important and timely? With a workforce of 8,000 technicians, even a small percentage of missed "Canceled" alerts represents a massive operational cost. The goal is to reduce missed critical notifications by 50% and ensure a response time of < 2 minutes for active jobs. Target Customer/Persona (The "Who") Field Technicians using Android mobile devices . Customer Outcomes / High-Level Requirements Sensory Differentiation: Technicians can identify a high-priority job update by sound and vibration alone, without looking at the screen. Critical Bypass: Users have the option to ensure critical work updates break through "Do Not Disturb" settings. User Scenarios in Scope As a technician driving to a job , I want a unique "Priority" sound to play if the job is canceled, so I can pull over safely or stop driving immediately. As a technician in a loud environment , I want a distinct vibration pattern for Dispatched jobs so I can feel the urgency even if I can't hear the phone. As a technician on a break , I want routine sync notifications to use the default sound so I am not unnecessarily interrupted. Out of Scope (i.e. Non-Goals) iOS Support: This release is strictly for the Android platform. Text-to-Speech: Read-aloud functionality for notification bodies is deferred. Logic Changes: No changes to the FSL "Drip-Feed" dispatching logic itself. Testing Hardware Diversity: Test haptic patterns across various Android device models to ensure "perceptible difference." State Testing: Verify that notifications correctly transition from "Default" to "Priority" sounds the moment a Service Appointment status changes to "Dispatched." OS Compatibility: Ensure full functionality on Android 8.0 through the latest current version. Acceptance Criteria Priority Trigger: Unique sound/haptic triggers only for Service Appointments and Work Orders in the "Dispatched" or "In-Progress" status category. Default Fallback: All other app notifications (e.g., data sync, future schedule updates) must use the system default settings. User Control: Technicians must be able to toggle sounds/haptics off via the Android System Settings for the specific app channels. Performance: Custom sounds must fire within 1 second of the notification being received by the device.
